Chrome Extension for SAP Integration Suite Version 1.0.0 by Goutham

Search and Monitor SAP Cloud Integration, Without Leaving the Page

CPI LogLens opens a panel directly on your SAP Integration Suite tenant. Search inside message payloads, review Message Processing Logs, check JMS and Data Store entries, and read API Management traffic in your active browser session.

The Payload Search workspace: search inside MPL attachments, Data Store entries, and JMS messages directly on your tenant.

How It Works

One Panel, Your Existing Session

CPI LogLens does not introduce a separate login or a separate server. It works entirely inside the tab you already have open.

01

It Opens On Your Tenant Page

The panel is injected into SAP Integration Suite pages at any https://*.hana.ondemand.com/* host. Press Alt+Shift+L or click the toolbar icon to toggle it.

02

It Reads With Your Session

Every search and monitoring call runs with your active browser session cookies and permissions. No API keys, credentials, or service accounts to store.

03

It Keeps Settings On Your Device

Saved Views, Custom Status configurations, exclusions, and theme preferences stay in local extension storage. Nothing is sent to external servers.

Searching inside attachment payloads, filtering Message Processing Logs, and switching workspaces.

Animation is off because your system prefers reduced motion.

Workspaces

Four Workspaces, One Panel

Switch between four focused workspaces without leaving the SAP Integration Suite page.

Payload Search

Search Inside Payload Content

Search inside MPL attachments, Data Store entries, and JMS messages, individually or all at once.

  • Syntax: free text, phrases, wildcards, comma-separated OR terms, field:value, case-sensitive mode, and regular expressions.
  • Scope: search within Body, Headers, or Properties.
  • Viewer: raw or beautified payload view, with in-viewer search, match navigation, copy, and download.

Message Monitoring

Review Message Processing Logs

Search MPL metadata by status, integration flow, and a set of advanced identifiers, then view results in the layout that fits the task.

  • Filters: status, Custom Status, integration flow, message ID, correlation ID, package, artifact, sender, receiver, and application message type or ID.
  • Views: List, Dashboard, Grouped, and Daily Reporting.
  • Drill-down: error details, custom headers, related messages, and run history for a selected message.

JMS / Data Store

Find Entries That Need Attention

Enumerate JMS queue messages and Data Store entries, and surface the ones that are overdue or expiring soon.

  • Highlights: overdue and expiring soon entries, with a configurable window of 1 to 90 days.
  • Filters: source and status.
  • Payloads: view an entry's payload on demand.

API Management

Read API Traffic And Errors

Reads aggregated analytics from SAP's Analytics Service, with drill-down into a single API's behavior.

  • Metrics: traffic, trends, latency, errors, and breakdowns by API, method, response code, consumer, and provider.
  • Boundary: only aggregated analytics are read. Request and response content, headers, credentials, and user identity are never retrieved.
  • Export: CSV, Excel, JSON report, and Copy Summary.

Shared Tools

The Same Mechanics In Every Workspace

A few controls work the same way no matter which workspace you are in.

Time Range
The same Time Range control appears in the workspaces that filter by time, with quick ranges such as Today and Past 30 Days, adjustable minutes or days, and a custom start and end range.
Saved Views
Save a search or filter configuration and return to it later, instead of rebuilding it each time.
Custom Status And Exclusions
Define the Custom Status values your tenant uses, and exclude non-business integration flows, packages, or artifacts from monitoring views. Both are saved only in your browser and can be exported or imported as JSON.
Exports
CSV, Excel, a JSON report, Copy Summary, and a PNG capture, using whatever is currently loaded.
Quick Guide
An in-panel reference explaining what each workspace does and how to use it, opened from the help icon in the toolbar.

Getting Started

Install It, Then Open The Panel

  1. Install The Chrome Extension

    Add CPI LogLens from the Chrome Web Store, or load unpacked during evaluation.

  2. Sign In To SAP Integration Suite

    Use your tenant as you normally would. No separate account or service registration is needed.

  3. Open the Panel

    Click the toolbar icon in Chrome, or press Alt+Shift+L on your keyboard.

  4. Choose A Workspace

    Select Payload Search, Message Monitoring, JMS / Data Store, or API Management from the top bar.

Practical Guidance

  • Set the Time Range first. It has the biggest effect on how long a search takes in the workspaces that filter by time.
  • Use the search syntax to narrow results. Wildcards, field:value, comma-separated OR terms, and regex reduce round trips.
  • Use Saved Views, Custom Status, and exclusions for recurring work. Set them up once per tenant and export them as JSON for colleagues.

Privacy & Security

What Happens With Your Data

CPI LogLens works between your browser and your SAP tenant. There is no other server involved.

Your Session, Your Permissions

Data is read from your SAP Integration Suite tenant using your current browser session. What you see depends strictly on the roles assigned to your SAP user account.

No Analytics Or Tracking

Nothing is sent to the developer or to any third party. This website does not track visitors, collect telemetry, or load analytics scripts.

Settings Stay On Your Device

Theme preferences, Saved Views, Custom Status rules, and exclusions are kept in the browser's local extension storage on your device.

API Analytics Only

The API Management workspace reads aggregated analytics. It never reads request or response content, headers, credentials, or user identity.

Bounded Payload Handling

ZIP attachments are checked against defensive size limits before processing: 500 entries, 256 MB total, and 128 MB per individual entry.

Validated Cross-Page Messaging

The script that captures payloads validates message origin, source window, command type, and target integration flow before processing.

Browser Permissions Requested
Permission Why It Is Requested
https://*.hana.ondemand.com/* Required to display the panel on your SAP Integration Suite tenant pages and issue search requests against tenant APIs using your active session.
storage Keeps your settings, Saved Views, Custom Status configurations, and theme preferences locally on your device. Never transmitted externally.
scripting Injects the extension panel and bridge on matching SAP Integration Suite tenant tabs when opened.

Before you share screenshots, exports, or copied diagnostic reports, remove confidential or sensitive production data.

FAQ

Common Questions

What does CPI LogLens connect to?
It activates only on SAP Integration Suite tenant pages matching https://*.hana.ondemand.com/*. It does not communicate with external servers, proxies, or remote APIs.
Does it send any data outside my browser?
No. It communicates solely with your SAP tenant using your existing authenticated browser session. There are no tracking pixels, external collectors, or cloud backends.
Where are my settings and Saved Views stored?
In your browser's local extension storage (chrome.storage.local). They remain on your device and are never synced to an external cloud.
What does the API Management workspace actually read?
Aggregated analytics from SAP's Analytics Service only. It does not inspect request or response bodies, authorization headers, API keys, or user identities.
What happens with large payloads or attachments?
ZIP attachments are inspected with strict defensive limits (up to 500 entries, 256 MB total, 128 MB per entry). Payloads exceeding memory safeguards are highlighted with truncation indicators.
What permissions does the extension require, and why?
Three permissions: host access to https://*.hana.ondemand.com/* to show the panel on your tenant, storage for your Saved Views and preferences, and scripting to initialize the panel when requested.
Is there a keyboard shortcut?
Yes. Press Alt+Shift+L to toggle the panel on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
